newsitem.title: USA: Sierra evaluates Physician Corp charge.
newsitem.headline: Sierra evaluates Physician Corp charge.

text.p: Sierra Health Services Inc said it considered Physician Corp of America's announcement of a $60 million fourth-quarter charge to be an "adverse development" for the proposed merger of the two companies.
"The new actuarial report is an adverse development that we are seriously evaluating," Sierra Chief Executive Officer Anthony Marlon said in a statement issued late on Thursday.
"Once we understand the full implications of this situation, we will weigh our various alternatives, he added. "We plan to disclose additional details within two weeks."
In November, Sierra announced plans to merge with Physician Corp in a stock transaction.
Sierra shares were up 2-3/8 to 27-1/8 by midday Friday. Physician Corp shares had plummeted 3-3/4 to a 52-week low of 5-3/8.

On Friday, Pacific Corp corrected the amount of the charge to about $80 million, which will cover increased liability in its workers' compensation division. Initially, it said the charge would amount to $60 million.

The fourth-quarter charge comes on top of a $130 million charge taken in the third quarter relating to the same division and discontinued workers' compensation-related insurance coverage in November 1996.
The combined company would be the eighth-largest managed health-care company in the United States, with about 1.5 million customers from Nevada to Florida.
